locator: Chemisch Weekblad45, pp269–277; PDFpp3–8 §§1–2 and technical findings
inspectedText: Court appointed five technical experts in June1946. They examined eight pictures. Old supports and convincing cracks did not establish the top paint’s age. X-rays showed two distinct crack networks; underlying old paint had been covered. Van Meegeren described synthetic phenol-formaldehyde resin, heating and mechanical cracking. Examiners reproduced effects and compared seized materials with samples, including isolated binder and refractive indices. Cross-sections supported resin-bound upper paint. They concluded that the examined paintings could indeed be his work.
quality: Report by two court-appointed examiners, contemporary to the investigation. Dutch OCR checked against parsed passages; summaries translated, no purported courtroom transcript.
limitations: Methods and observations belong to the eight examined paintings; do not generalize every fake or reproduce later simplified X-ray claims.
Report combines van Meegeren’s explanation with experimental confirmation; pigment tests alone did not date these paintings.
Some color reactions alone were insufficient; isolated binder, optical comparison, cross-sections and material comparisons formed the evidence.
method: Actual web parsed source body/PDF passages inspected during this session, not search snippets. Selected passages only; entry time records retrieval session. Paraphrases and translations, no original full-body download implied.
